title: Shakespeare Dialogue Analysis
text:
Data collected from: https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/main/data/2024/2024-09-17/
Original data from: https://shakespeare.mit.edu/
This dataset shows dialogue from 3 of Shakespeare’s plays: Hamlet, Macbeth, and Romeo and Juliet. This project looks at how word usage differs between plays, which characters speak the most, and how frequently certain themes appear.

title: Shakespeare Dialogue Analysis
text:
Loading data


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)

hamlet <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-09-17/hamlet.csv")

macbeth <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-09-17/macbeth.csv")

romeo_juliet <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-09-17/romeo_juliet.csv")

plays <- bind_rows(
  hamlet |> mutate(play = "Hamlet"),
  macbeth |> mutate(play = "Macbeth"),
  romeo_juliet |> mutate(play = "Romeo and Juliet")
)

plays <- plays |>
  filter(!is.na(dialogue), !is.na(character)) |>
  filter(!str_detect(character, regex("stage direction", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(
    dialogue = str_squish(dialogue),
    character = str_to_title(character),
    play = factor(play, levels = c("Hamlet", "Macbeth", "Romeo and Juliet")),
    word_count = str_count(dialogue, "\\b[A-Za-z]+\\b")
  )

title: Food Beverages
text:
Data collected from: https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-05-05
Original data from: https://www.istat.it/


Code
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))


This dataset gives data on industrial production of food and beverages, transport equipment, and textiles over a period of 100 years.


Code
food_beverages <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-05-05/food_beverages.csv', show_col_types = FALSE)

ggplot(food_beverages, aes(x = Year, y = Sugar)) +
    geom_point() + 
    labs(
        x = "Year",
        y = "Sugar produced (tons)",
        title = "Sugar production levels over the years"
    )









We can see that over the years, sugar production levels have continued to increase, with each decade almost always surpassing the previous decade in production.

title: Penguins
text:
Data collected from: https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-07-14
Original data from: https://opentraits.org/datasets/avonet.html


Code
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))


This dataset gives morphometric data for 18 species of penguins within 6 genera. In total, 93 penguins were surveyed.


Code
many_penguins <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-07-14/many_penguins.csv', show_col_types = FALSE)


ggplot(many_penguins, aes(x = beak.width, y = beak.length_culmen)) +
    geom_point() + 
    labs(
        x = "Beak width (mm)",
        y = "Culmen length (mm)",
        title = "Penguin beak width to culmen length relation"
    ) +
        facet_wrap(~species)









We can see that, for 6 of the species, there is little variation of culmen length and beak width. However, some species, such as eudyptes robustus. have quite a large variation in their culmen length and beak width. Overall, there is little relation between the two measurements.
